manifesto.heading: Build. Then verify.
paragraphs: Most claims about software are never tested, not just infrastructure. A controller advertises self-healing, a chart declares a probe, a tool says it can catch a leak — and in almost every repository those sentences are taken on trust, because checking them costs a real afternoon and nobody is asking.

So I break my own systems on purpose. I scale a deployment by hand against a live cluster to see whether reconciliation actually reverts it, or point a synthesised policy at a database that isn't mine to prove it actually withholds rows, because a system that has never been contradicted looks exactly like one that cannot be. What I publish is not the claim. It is the test, the result, and the list of cases the test does not cover.
